mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES mobility is a leading indicator of more in-person shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks as commuting restores weekday retail traffic.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains above its last-4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in TRANSIT usage reduces friction for discretionary trips and supports short-horizon increases in retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC should improve within one week after transit begins recovering.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within the next 7 days after TRANSIT posts two consecutive weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility remains elevated while WORKPLACES stay depressed, shopping consolidates into local neighborhood trips rather than destination retail, so RETAIL_REC falls relative to the prior month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds WORKPLACES by at least 20 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying at least 20 points above WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both continue trending upward together, it signals broader reopening and spillover to discretionary shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over 28 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES are above their prior-4-week means.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp relative shift from outdoor leisure back to travel and errands is captured by declining PARKS and rising TRANSIT; that combination should precede a higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below its 2-week average while TRANSIT rises above its 2-week average
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS weakens and TRANSIT strengthens simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: In a summer reopening regime, persistently positive PARKS mobility competes with mall and street retail time, so sustained PARKS strength should suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS remains above zero and does not weaken from its recent level.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains more than 40 percent below baseline, it indicates ongoing access constraints that keep discretionary shopping depressed, so RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over 28 days even though TRANSIT remains below -40 for the full period.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising GROCERY_PHARM and falling RESIDENTIAL implies more out-of-home errand clustering and less home-stay substitution, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while RESIDENTIAL falls week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week.
